newsitem.title: INDIA: Egypt, India vow to foster closer economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, India vow to foster closer economic ties.

text.p: Egypt and India pledged on Wednesday to forge closer trade and investment ties aimed at strengthening two of Asia's and Africa's largest emerging economies, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said.

Moussa, who arrived in India at the weekend for a meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement, told a business conference that his nation and India were poised to seize the opportunities thrown up by six years of economic reforms in both countries.
"The economic and trade relations that currently exist between us do neither reflect the reality of both countries emerging nor the historic and friendly ties that are binding us together," he said.
Egypt, which in 1961 allied with India in launching the Non-Aligned Movement, is the south Asian country's largest African trading partner.
Indian Foreign Ministry officials said President Hosni Mubarak was due to visit India later this year.
Moussa met Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral earlier on Wednesday.
The two ministers were due to sign treaties on investment protection and promotion, science and technology, civil aviation, tourism and media cooperation later on Wednesday.
India and Egypt also agreed to set up a joint commission to facilitate investment and trade and exchanges in the fields of science, technology and culture.
Moussa urged Indian businessmen to invest in his country, particularly in a new project establishing a new valley parallel to the Nile, built on two million acres of reclaimed land.
"It will be up for investment in the areas of tourism, road building, airports, and construction," he said.

"We certainly need more investment -- just as you here in India need more investment. We believe that both countries have a lot to achieve together either bilaterally as well as in the context of South-South cooperation," Moussa said.
